title: Keyword Token Rules with Negative Lookahead
description: Read the ten keyword (name, regex) tuple entries that use (?!\w) to prevent matching identifier prefixes.

steps.description: Lines 1-4 define the `(name, pattern)` tuples for `"WHILE"`, `"PRINT"`, `"TRUE"`, and `"FALSE"`, where each keyword literal is followed by the negative lookahead `(?!\w)`.
Look at `(?!\w)` at the end of `r"while(?!\w)"` on line 1: it asserts that the character immediately after `while` is not a word character (`[A-Za-z0-9_]`), without consuming that next character.

steps.question: If the scanner tests `("OR", r"or(?!\w)")` (line 6) at the start of `"order"` versus `"or(x)"`, which input matches `OR` and why?
steps.answer: `"or(x)"` matches `OR` because `'('` is not a word character (`\w`), whereas `"order"` fails `(?!\w)` because `'d'` is a word character, leaving `"order"` to match `IDENT`.

steps.description: Lines 5-10 apply the same `(?!\w)` suffix to the boolean operators (`"AND"`, `"OR"`, `"NOT"`) and control-flow keywords (`"FUN"`, `"BREAK"`, `"CONTINUE"`).
At trace step 0 on line 1, Python evaluates the tuple `('WHILE', 'while(?!\\w)')`.
